Summarize the document below in at most 120 words for an executive who has not read it. State only facts that appear in it.

Incident report INC-2291. On 14 March at 09:12 UTC the payments API began returning 429 errors. Root cause: a nightly export job introduced on 12 March ran against the primary storage account and consumed 80 percent of its request quota; a retry loop in the checkout service amplified the load. Impact: 41 minutes of degraded checkout, 3,870 failed orders and an estimated 52,000 dollars in delayed revenue; no data was lost. Detection: an alert fired at 09:19 but was routed to a retired on-call group, so a human noticed only at 09:31 from customer support reports. Mitigation: the export job was paused at 09:44 and the retry loop capped at three attempts. Contributing factors: no load test covered the export job, the quota dashboard had no alert, and the on-call rotation had not been updated after the team reorganization on 1 March. Follow-ups: move the export to a read replica by 28 March (owner Priya), add a quota alert at 60 percent by 21 March (owner Marcus), audit all alert routing by 4 April (owner Priya), and add export jobs to the quarterly load-test plan. The team decided not to roll back the checkout release because it was unrelated to the cause.

Summarize the document below in at most 120 words for an executive who has not read it. State only facts that appear in it.

Memo: tagging policy rollout. Effective 1 June, all new Azure resources must carry four tags: owner, cost-center, environment and data-class. Resources missing tags will be created in a non-compliant state and flagged in the weekly report; from 1 September the policy effect changes from Audit to Deny for production subscriptions only. Development and sandbox subscriptions stay on Audit until further notice. Existing resources have until 31 August to be remediated; the platform team will provide a script and two office-hour sessions per week in June. Exceptions require approval from the cloud governance board and are valid for 90 days. The expected effort is about four hours per application team. Rationale: 23 percent of last quarter's spend, roughly 410,000 dollars, could not be attributed to a team. Questions go to the cloud-governance channel. The data-class tag accepts three values: public, internal and restricted.

Summarize the document below in at most 120 words for an executive who has not read it. State only facts that appear in it.

Weekly platform sync. Dana opened by saying the Kubernetes upgrade to 1.31 is on track for 22 April. Luis raised that two internal apps still use a deprecated API and may break; Dana agreed to block the upgrade for those namespaces until they are fixed. Priya reported that the cost report shows a 12 percent drop in compute spend after right-sizing, saving about 18,000 dollars a month. Luis asked whether the number includes the reserved instance purchase; Priya said it does not and will rerun the analysis. Marcus proposed switching the CI runners to spot instances, estimating a 40 percent saving but noting a risk of job interruption; the group decided to pilot it on the documentation pipeline only, for four weeks, before any wider move. Dana asked about the monitoring migration; Marcus said it is blocked on a licensing quote that has not arrived, with no date. Actions: Luis to list affected apps by Friday; Priya to rerun the cost analysis next week; Marcus to set up the spot pilot; Dana to chase the licensing quote.
